events.text:
Entry contract: v50, 2026-10-09.

| 📍 **q-0027** · How does each turn know its next step, and each session where to resume? |
|---|

Hello again. The wake is in. This conversation stands on q-0027 until you name the work.

Landed work whose boxes are still open comes first.[^1] Two tickets share that rank, so both are here.

- [01-0010.0174 each hook finds its interpreter](docs/tickets/01-0010.0174-each-hook-finds-its-interpreter.md) was implemented on 2026-10-09. Three boxes are open: the hooks deliver the window on a clone with no `uv`, each of the three hosts runs them in a live Windows session, and `/verify`. A running session already stands on q-0018.0020.0005.0002 How does each hook find a working interpreter in every clone, under each host's shell? That ticket stays with it.
- [01-0011.0110.0020 a paragraph shows what it stands on](docs/tickets/01-0011.0110.0020-a-paragraph-shows-what-it-stands-on.md) was verified on 2026-10-08. Two boxes wait on a week of your grading. Running sessions stand on q-0030 How does a reply show the principles each of its claims stands on, and where are the principles named for it?

The queue’s candidate, once you nod, is [01-0011.0110.0040.0010 every record shows what it is a record of](docs/tickets/01-0011.0110.0040.0010-every-record-shows-what-it-is-a-record-of.md). It is Ready, AFK, and its next step is `/plan`. It answers q-0024.0009.0003.0001 How does every record an agent edits show what it is a record of? One decision also waits at `/align`: q-0026.0003 What does an entry-contract version cover?

Three occasions since that order was set are yours to promote or leave.[^2]

1. On 2026-10-09 you took issue 4 ahead of the queue. The merge has landed. [01-0010.0176 a failed install gate says why it failed](docs/tickets/01-0010.0176-a-failed-gate-says-why.md) is Ready and AFK, and the hooks session’s handoff names it as that session’s next. The queue’s candidate remains `.0040.0010`.
2. [Session 45](docs/sessions/0045-20261009-what-the-harness-is-for.md) asks whether goals derived from the product document, and [01-0010.0150 the harness meets a tree that already has a method](docs/tickets/01-0010.0150-harness-meets-a-tree-with-a-method.md), should become the candidate.
3. [Session 44, the roots](docs/sessions/0044-20261009-a-store-opens-with-three-roots.md), left two questions from that work for you, and called [01-0011.0100.0050 a question branches before it is answered](docs/tickets/01-0011.0100.0050-a-question-branches-before-it-is-answered.md) the queue’s next. The candidate paragraph names `.0040.0010`, with `.0050` after those slices.

I stop at this fork. The next cycle waits for your nod. (💡 *Human checkpoints*)

Ten other sessions are marked running. Five stand on a question: the interpreter ticket, the merge’s child (that ticket has since closed), q-0018.0020.0003 How does a first install end with the project’s own verification set?, and q-0030 with a child. Five have no position. Nothing is suspect, and no straw dog is due. Two deferrals were re-checked; their conditions are unmet. q-0001.0013 How does the store remember every id it has given, so none is given twice? waits on a stale id landing silently. q-0006 Could the rule set be composite, with no pure core anywhere? waits on a second mechanism whose rules cannot be injected as a block.

The tree is clean apart from `docs/questions/sessions`, the store’s session rows, including this one.

| | |
|---|---|
| ⚖️ Decisions | Which item this session takes. Also still waiting: the grading week on 01-0011.0110.0020, and q-0026.0003 at `/align`. |
| 🍂 Drift | [Delivery status](docs/tickets/README.md): the completed-step chronicle ends at session 42 on 2026-10-08, and the verification-set line still says 532 tests on 2026-10-05. Session 44 recorded 572 at its close on 2026-10-09. Left as found. |
| 🪢 Tangle | Two records are both numbered 0044, and several sessions are writing this tree at once. q-0032 How do sessions running at once in one tree keep from overwriting each other’s writes? is open. Left unresolved. |

[^1]: [pacer.md](docs/pacer.md), Core rules — the user, 2026-09-06. A tie at one rank is presented. (💡 *Do not reopen an accepted decision without new evidence*)
[^2]: The queue’s order, the user, 2026-09-27, reconfirmed 2026-09-29; the candidate set to `.0040.0010` on 2026-10-08, in the delivery status. A last session’s handoff is a list of candidates. The queue states the order.
